Sunday June 7, 2026 morning. June 7 morning opens on the most consequential single-day watching window of the current negotiating cycle: the Sunday signing window. Reporting from the June 6 close identified Sunday June 7 as a candidate signing target for the Iran MOU amendment — Trump's counter-demand issued June 5 requiring immediate Hormuz transfer and tighter nuclear terms. Today simultaneously marks Hormuz Day 100 — a strategic and symbolic inflection point at 100 consecutive days of Strait closure, estimated $25–30B cumulative US military cost, Brent sustained above $90, and global shipping disruption now embedded in Q2 inflation readings. The private diplomatic channel remains confirmed open (Iran comms resolved Day 4, no re-suspension signal). Reporting characterizes the US as adjusting its negotiating position toward Iranian demands — the most concrete framework-adjustment signal of the counter-demand period. Ghalibaf's June 6 'missiles not talks' statement enters Day 2 without retraction or escalation into ultimatum territory, preserving the public-private bifurcation. The day's conditional architecture is clear: confirmed Iran signing = immediate Vibe upgrade to 4 or 5; formal rejection = Vibe 2.

vibe.rationale: Vibe 3 — lower edge, conditional upside. June 7 morning opens at 3, holding the position established at the June 6 evening close. The Sunday signing window is the single highest-priority watch item of the day: if Iran formally accepts the MOU amendment counter-demand and a signing is confirmed, Vibe upgrades immediately to 4 (Beirut truce holding, comms intact) or 5 (full signing with Hormuz timeline clarity and both principals committed). The conditions sustaining Vibe 3 at morning open: (1) Iran comms remain resolved — Day 4, no re-suspension signal — the private channel is structurally open, which is the sine qua non of continued deal compression; (2) reporting characterizes the US as adjusting its negotiating position toward Iranian demands — the deal compression framing is intact rather than collapsed; (3) Ghalibaf Day 2 without retraction or escalation to ultimatum — the public-private bifurcation remains operative; (4) Beirut-suburbs partial truce Day 4 overnight clean — longest operative hold of the Lebanon track; (5) CENTCOM self-defense authority operative, no kinetic resumption in the June 6–7 overnight cycle. Four factors prevent morning upgrade to 4: (1) no confirmed signing as of this report — the Sunday window is open, not resolved; (2) Mojtaba Khamenei's non-approval of the amended MOU text persists as the structural bottleneck — no courier-route confirmation signal as of morning; (3) Ghalibaf's 'missiles not talks' statement remains unretracted at Day 2, sustaining the public hardline as the dominant Iranian visible posture; (4) Hormuz Day 100 is a symbolic threshold that creates domestic hardening pressure on both principals, not a de-escalation catalyst in itself. Upgrade to 4 requires: confirmed signing or both-party confirmed new concrete timeline for MOU amendment; Beirut truce Day 5 clean. Upgrade to 5 requires: signed MOU with Hormuz transfer timeline operative. Drop to 2 requires: Iran formal rejection of amendment counter-demand; Ghalibaf or Khamenei escalation to ultimatum tier; CENTCOM repositioning signal; Lebanon partial truce collapse.

items.headline: NSF Ocean Observatories Going Dark Off PNW Coast — Last Newport OR Station by June End; T-HUD -10.4% Enacted Path; Battery Storage Surge Nationally; Grid Modernization Lagging AI Demand; Sound Transit $34.5B Gap
items.summary: Four secondary infrastructure threads entering June 7. First: the National Science Foundation has removed all floating ocean observatories from Washington coastal waters (three stations off Grays Harbor, removed September 2025) and is removing the last remaining Oregon station (off Newport) by end of June 2026, as part of the national Trump administration dismantling of Pacific and Atlantic ocean data buoy networks. For PNW operational contexts, the removal degrades: atmospheric river early detection (primary winter storm trigger mechanism), real-time ocean temperature data for fisheries and marine heat wave forecasting, wave height and storm surge data for coastal emergency management, and Pacific maritime traffic monitoring at a moment when Hormuz-disrupted rerouting has elevated Pacific corridor traffic volumes. The degradation is structural and permanent absent federal policy reversal. Second: T-HUD full committee markup at $92.224B (-10.4% from FY26) — the enacted-path baseline for transit capital, CDBG, and Amtrak — has not advanced to House floor scheduling. Sound Transit's $34.5B funding gap remains unresolved heading into the board's June capital planning session. Sound Transit's Link Light Rail is the primary transit mode for Lumen Field access during the FIFA World Cup beginning June 15. Third: nationally, battery storage deployment is accelerating — year-to-date 2025 installations exceeded 2024's full-year 10 GW record; 2026 trajectory tracking significantly above that pace, providing growing grid backstop function. But the 224 GW AI data center incremental load forecast through 2035 continues outpacing battery storage and transmission modernization capacity. Fourth: FERC summer assessment confirms PNW drought-reduced hydropower as a specific summer grid vulnerability; SPP, PJM, and CAISO retain sufficient summer capacity for expected demand but identify wildfire-drought-heat as tail-risk scenarios.

The study creates a procedural pathway for the Trump administration to restrict access; formal restriction would require the safety study to identify a specific adverse signal, but initiation opens the regulatory mechanism. The Santos-Kalshi investigation is the first high-profile allegation of prediction market manipulation by a public figure and will inform regulatory posture toward platforms that have become consequential in political event pricing. Fourth: SCOTUS Alabama redistricting ruling (lower court reversed, expanded state redistricting latitude) remains operative in multiple states' 2026 electoral map calculations. California Governor primary: Becerra, Porter, Steyer (Democratic); Bianco, Hilton (Republican) — advancing through primary cycle.

analyst_summary: June 7, 2026 morning opens at Vibe 3 — lower edge, conditional upside architecture. The day is defined by a single highest-priority binary: the Sunday Iran MOU signing window. If Iran formally accepts the amendment counter-demand (immediate Hormuz transfer, tighter nuclear terms) and a signing is confirmed today, the Vibe upgrades immediately to 4 or 5 and the deal-confirmation trade activates across oil, equities, and late-2026 rate expectations. If the window passes without signing, the amendment counter-demand phase extends into an additional week at maximum 'delay not collapse' interpretive pressure, and the Monday Brent opening becomes the next read on market conviction. The factors sustaining 3 this morning: Iran comms resolved Day 4 (private channel structurally open); US adjusting position toward Iranian demands (deal compression framing intact); Ghalibaf Day 2 without retraction or ultimatum (bifurcation preserved); Beirut suburbs partial truce Day 4 overnight clean (Lebanon track stable); CENTCOM operative, no kinetic resumption. Hormuz Day 100 is today's strategic milestone — 100 days of closure, $25–30B cumulative US cost, Brent above $90 — arriving without a new escalation signal. Armenia elections underway; Peru runoff today — both results tonight. Warsh Day 24 silent with 9 days to the June 16–17 inaugural FOMC; rate environment unchanged. DHS/ICE House floor action targets the week of June 9; Reconciliation 2.0 July 4 deadline 27 days out without a floor date. Measles dispersal Day 2 in full summer mobile phase — CDC summer travel warning active. NIFC above-normal Day 7; Oregon 83% drought; Washington drought emergency Day 3 (4th consecutive year); east Cascades above-normal fuel drying advancing toward July onset; NIFC-FIFA co-response risk window T-4. NSF ocean observatories going dark off the PNW coast by month's end — permanent structural monitoring degradation. This morning's watch architecture reduces to one primary question and two secondary: (1) Iran: does the Sunday window produce a confirmed signing? (2) Armenia: does Pashinyan secure the projected majority, reducing South Caucasus second-order risk? (3) Peru: Fujimori or Sánchez — results arriving tonight shape Andean critical minerals diplomacy.
